_comment: Copy-editing and mis-pairing fixes for the published programming. HQ's PDFs carry typos, spacing slips and — occasionally — a coaching note pasted from a different movement. These are re-applied automatically on every merge (see apply_text_corrections in src/text_corrections.py), so re-parsing a month's PDF can't silently undo them. Nothing here changes a workout: only prose, exercise names, and notes that belong to a different exercise. Every entry records what the source says and why it was changed.

replacements.find: drop back knee to to ground
replacements.replace: drop back knee to the ground

replacements.why: number run into the following word
comma immediately followed by a full stop
a sentence starting lower-case after a full stop

note_overrides.note_startswith: Holding 1 KB opposite of front leg
note_overrides.new_note: Hinge slightly and hold the end of the bar at chest height with both hands. Turn through the hips and ribs together, arms staying long, and control the bar back across.
note_overrides.why: The published note describes a KB drop split squat — the same sentence appears on 'KB Drop Split Squat' on 11/20. Replaced with a note for the movement actually named.

note_overrides.note_startswith: Create tension, slowly pull into deep squat position
note_overrides.new_note: Step straight back and drop the back knee toward the floor, torso tall. Drive through the whole front foot to stand, and alternate sides.
note_overrides.why: The published note describes a deep prying squat — the same sentence appears on 'BW Squat' on 08/17. Replaced with a note for the movement actually named.

note_overrides.new_note: Lie back on the incline bench with a DB in each hand and a slight bend in the elbows. Open the arms wide as though hugging the ceiling, then bring them back together over the chest.
note_overrides.why: The published note describes a kettlebell row, not an incline fly.

note_overrides.note_startswith: Lying on bench. Hold DB with both hands
note_overrides.new_note: Stand on the band with a handle in each hand, palms up. Curl to the shoulders keeping the elbows pinned to the ribs, then lower under control.
note_overrides.why: The published note describes a DB pullover — the same sentence appears on 'DB Pullover' on 11/20.

note_overrides.note_startswith: DB in goblet position, sitting deep into squat
note_overrides.new_note: Hold the DB in the goblet position. Step wide to one side, pushing the hips back with the trailing leg straight, then push back to the middle and alternate.
note_overrides.why: The published note describes a goblet squat — the same sentence appears on 'Heels Elevated Goblet Squat' on 09/07.

note_overrides.new_note: Sit in the 90/90 position, drive the front knee into the ground and keep the chest tall and reaching forward over the front leg.
note_overrides.why: The published note is a jump-landing cue, which belongs to the squat-jump row directly below it on the same page (both rows are labelled 1e in the source).

renames.from: Elevated Goblet Squat Band Tall Kneeling X
renames.why: The row above has a four-line name that overflows its cell, so the tail of it lands in this row's name. This row's own note and demo video are both the tall-kneeling band pulldown.
Same overflow, seen from the other side: this row's name is cut short where it spills into the row below. Its demo video is the heels-elevated landmine goblet squat.
